title: The day after your miracle dies feels quieter than the crucifixion.
paragraphs: The day after your miracle dies feels quieter than the crucifixion.
That’s Luke 24:21 energy.

Not loud grief.
Not public chaos.
Just two broken disciples walking the road with this ache in their chest: “We had hoped…”
And that line is where many people live.

We had hoped the marriage would survive.
We had hoped the child would come home.
We had hoped the prayer would be answered by now.
We had hoped Jesus would do something before everything fell apart.
That’s the pain of Luke 24. Not just sorrow.
Disappointment.

Because Jesus was not only loved. He was expected. They thought He would redeem Israel. They thought the story was going somewhere glorious. Instead, the cross happened. The tomb happened. Silence happened.

The day after everything fell apart is dangerous, kapatid, because that’s the day people start rewriting what God meant.
They call a delay a denial.
They call a grave the end.
They call shattered expectations the absence of God.
But here’s what we miss:
Jesus was closest to them when they thought hope was gone.

On the road to Emmaus, the risen Christ walked beside confused, grieving, disappointed disciples who did not even recognize Him. That means you can be heartbroken, disoriented, and still be standing inside a miracle you haven’t understood yet.
Read that again.
The resurrection had already happened while they were still talking like heaven had failed.
That will preach.

Some of you are interpreting Friday while Jesus is already living in Sunday.
Some of you are mourning a closed chapter while Christ is opening eternity.
Some of you think your faith died, but really, your assumptions died.
And yes, that hurts.

Because God will sometimes let the version of hope you created collapse so He can give you the real one anchored in Christ, not in your timeline, not in your preferred outcome, not in your fantasy of how redemption should look.
Luke 24:21 is not the end of the story. It is the sentence spoken before burning hearts, opened eyes, and resurrected certainty.
So if today feels like the day after everything fell apart, hear me clearly:

Jesus is not absent from your ruins.
He is walking in them.
Explaining Himself in them.
Revealing glory through them.
And in His perfect time, He will cause your heart to burn again.
Your “we had hoped” is not stronger than His resurrection.

Repent of burying your hope in outcomes.
Put your hope back in Christ alone.

Because the gospel is this: our sin deserved death, Jesus bore that death, and He rose again so the shattered, ashamed, confused, and broken would not stay buried with their disappointment. In Him, despair does not get the final word.
Resurrection does.
